name: Ecofeminism
summary: Ecofeminism holds that the domination of women and the domination of nonhuman nature are linked, through patriarchal conceptual dualisms (man/woman, culture/nature, mind/body) and through institutions such as capitalism, mechanistic science and patriarchal religion. It seeks an ecological, care-based and often subsistence-oriented alternative to growth-driven development, and it is expressed through grassroots women's environmental activism and anti-militarism. Strands differ on whether the women-nature link is socially constructed or reflects embodied experience, and on spirituality.
scope: The mainstream academic and activist ecofeminism since d'Eaubonne's 1974 coinage, centred on Karen Warren's logic of domination, Carolyn Merchant, Val Plumwood, and the materialist/Global South strand of Vandana Shiva and Maria Mies. It spans the social/socialist, vegetarian and spiritual strands; where they differ, answers follow the socialist and Shiva-Mies core and mark contested points low.

keyFigures.name: Francoise d'Eaubonne
keyFigures.role: French writer who coined the term ecofeminism in 1974.

keyFigures.name: Vandana Shiva
keyFigures.role: Author of Staying Alive and co-author of Ecofeminism; leading voice of the Global South materialist strand.

keyFigures.name: Karen J. Warren
keyFigures.role: Philosopher who formulated the logic of domination and ecological feminist ethics.

sources.author: Environment & Society Portal
sources.usedFor: The term's origin and the claim that patriarchal suppression of women parallels suppression of nature.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not a core ecofeminist topic; care ethics and attention to health harms of pollution suggest support for public provision.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Inferred from concern for women's low-paid and undervalued labour; the sources do not discuss wage floors.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Shiva argues the market organises resource use through demand that ignores nature's and women's sustenance economy, so markets allocate badly.

public-ownership.rationale: Adherents split between socialist ecofeminists and commons or community-control advocates who distrust the state as much as the market.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Inferred from the materialist strand's critique of capitalist inequality; taxation itself is rarely discussed.

unions-good.rationale: Inferred from the social/socialist strand's attention to labour; unions are not a central ecofeminist topic.

property-fundamental.rationale: Ecofeminists note that women and nature are both treated as property, and Shiva defends commons against enclosure, so absolute property rights are rejected.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Corporate profit-driven exploitation of nature is a central target, and regulation or curbing of corporate power follows from that critique.

cut-welfare.rationale: The materialist strand stresses the undervaluation of social reproduction and care, so cutting welfare is opposed.

worker-ownership.rationale: Socialist ecofeminists favour democratic control of production, but the emphasis is on community and subsistence production more than worker firms.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred from feminist and grassroots distrust of state security power; not discussed in the sources.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Ecofeminism has no settled position on drug policy.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Adherents are split; intersectional concern for harms of discrimination coexists with distrust of state power. Not addressed in sources.

strong-leader.rationale: Ecofeminism favours decentred, grassroots power (Shiva's 'decentred powers') and opposes masculinist domination, so a strongman is rejected.

state-harmful.rationale: Critical of the state as an agent of maldevelopment, but most ecofeminists do not call for abolishing it.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred from the movement's feminist anti-militarism (such as the Women's Pentagon Actions); gun control is not discussed.

empower-police-military.rationale: Ecofeminist activism includes anti-militarist protest such as the Women's Pentagon Actions, and militarism is read as a form of masculinist domination.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Feminists, and so ecofeminists, are divided between decriminalisation and abolitionist views.

decide-locally.rationale: Shiva favours decentred, local control of resources and local knowledge, with local consumption for local needs.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from nonviolence and care emphasis; criminal justice is not discussed.

traditional-family.rationale: Ecofeminism challenges patriarchal structures, though some strands value caregiving roles; the family itself is not a central topic.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Queer ecologies grew out of ecofeminism and its critique of dualisms, implying support; marriage law is not a stated position.

abortion-legal.rationale: Feminist concern with women's reproductive autonomy; some strands criticise reproductive technology, which lowers certainty.

more-religion-public.rationale: Patriarchal religions are named as a driver of ecological crisis, though spiritual ecofeminists favour earth-based spirituality, not public religion.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The movement originated in women linking race, class and gender with environmental harm and engages environmental racism directly.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Most ecofeminists see the gender dualisms as culturally constructed, though some strands emphasise embodied difference.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Ecofeminism focuses on local and indigenous knowledge rather than national culture; nationalism is not a theme.

gradual-change.rationale: Ecofeminists seek deep restructuring of economy and knowledge, not incremental respect for established institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Inferred from solidarity with Global South women and justice orientation; not discussed in sources.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Shiva criticises international development institutions as imposing maldevelopment, though global cooperation is not rejected.

free-trade.rationale: Shiva argues export-market integration diverts land and resources from subsistence and harms women and the poor.

nation-first.rationale: Ecofeminism stresses global ecological and justice links but is not a nationalist-versus-globalist debate.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Anti-militarism suggests scepticism about military intervention; the topic is not directly discussed.

open-borders.rationale: No stated ecofeminist position; solidarity themes pull one way, local-community emphasis the other.

limit-growth.rationale: Shiva states that the GNP growth called development is maldevelopment that destroys nature and women's sustenance work, and calls for recovering regenerative alternatives.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Ecological crisis is the movement's core concern, and activists call for fundamental change rather than mild measures.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Mies and Shiva critique the philosophical foundations of modern science and technology; Shiva calls reductionist science patriarchal and violent.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anti-nuclear and anti-militarist activism is part of the movement; nuclear power is read as masculinist high technology.

revolution-justified.rationale: Strands differ; the movement emphasises nonviolent grassroots action over revolution, and the topic is not addressed.

experts-over-public.rationale: Warren and Shiva challenge detached expert knowers and defend local women's knowledge against experts.

central-planning.rationale: Shiva criticises centralised development planning, but socialist ecofeminists are not market advocates either.

socialized-markets.rationale: Socialist ecofeminists might accept it, while subsistence advocates prefer to limit markets; not a stated position.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not discussed by ecofeminist sources and no principle clearly decides it.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from the materialist critique of inequality; not discussed.

basic-income.rationale: Inferred from the push to value unpaid care and subsistence work; not discussed directly.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Shiva favours protecting local subsistence economies, but the industrial-protection framing is not hers.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Shiva criticises state-led development projects, and nothing in the sources endorses strategic state investment.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Favours small-scale local producers and commons over corporate or state concentration, though property as such is questioned.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Mies and Shiva favour subsistence production with reciprocity replacing commodity relations, but abolition of money and wages is not a stated programme.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Opposes market-led money logic and commodification, but central banks are not discussed.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Not discussed; decentred grassroots power is favoured over state-recognised corporate bodies.

one-party-rule.rationale: Shiva's decentred, grassroots politics and the movement's critique of hierarchy exclude single-party rule.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Opposition to patriarchy and hereditary hierarchy; monarchy is not discussed directly.

democracy-best.rationale: Grassroots democratic activism is central, but ecofeminists do not stress defending democracy against bad voter choices.

direct-votes.rationale: Participatory, grassroots politics suggests support, though referendums are not discussed.

workers-councils.rationale: Socialist strand might favour them, but the movement as a whole centres communities and women's movements, not councils.

right-to-secede.rationale: Not discussed; no principle decides it.

natural-rulers.rationale: The framework of the logic of domination rejects the claim that superiority justifies rule over others.

political-violence-never.rationale: Nonviolence is a stated value, particularly in spiritual strands and Chipko-style protest, but adherents are not uniformly absolute.

war-builds-character.rationale: Militarism is treated as masculinist domination, and the movement protests war.

separate-church-state.rationale: Patriarchal religions are criticised, but spiritual ecofeminists value religious expression; the question of church-state is not addressed.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Patriarchal religion is named as one of four forces behind the ecological crisis.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Privatising public goods runs against the movement's critique of commodification.

military-superiority.rationale: Anti-militarist activism, such as the Women's Pentagon Actions, opposes military buildup.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The movement is built on intersecting critiques of race, class and gender, and rejects domination based on group hierarchy.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Materialist ecofeminists give class weight, but the movement treats gender and ecology as co-primary.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Concern for inequality is strong, but equal outcomes as a goal is not stated.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Ecofeminists honour indigenous and local land-based knowledge and activism, such as the Akwesasne project, and defend communities' control of resources.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Shiva treats colonialism as a driver of maldevelopment, which suggests support, but reparations are not stated.

civilizational-union.rationale: Not discussed; ecofeminism is oriented to global justice and local community.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The ethic of care and relational ethics reject self-interest as a moral foundation.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Care ethics stresses responsibilities, but rights language is also used and the question is not addressed.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Warren draws on a land ethic and Shiva treats nature as a source of life; SEP presents ecological feminism as extending moral concern to nonhuman nature.

limit-population.rationale: Population is not discussed in the SEP entry, and Shiva locates scarcity in maldevelopment more than in numbers, so mild opposition is inferred.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Shiva calls industrial maldevelopment destructive of nature and women, but the claim of disaster for humanity overall is stronger than most state.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Shiva criticises modern technology and biotechnology as patriarchal projects; speeding disruption is opposed.

human-enhancement.rationale: Spretnak's agenda criticises reproductive technology, suggesting scepticism; the topic is inferred.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Inferred from criticism of technocratic detached knowledge; Salleh addresses digitalisation critically.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: No stated position; privacy concerns and state distrust are not developed in the sources.

restore-past-order.rationale: The movement seeks transformation of patriarchal order, though it values recovering older ecological and subsistence knowledge.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The movement is explicitly values-driven and critical of supposed neutrality.

direct-action.rationale: Documented examples include Chipko tree-hugging, the Green Belt Movement and the Women's Pentagon Actions, though elections are not rejected.

means-match-ends.rationale: Nonviolence and care are both means and ends in the movement; Shiva ties methods to the recovery of life-sustaining principles.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Shiva praises subsistence agriculture and sustainable livelihoods, not hunter-gatherer return.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: The movement criticises gendered division of labour but does not call for abolishing division of labour in general.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Shiva emphasises production for basic needs and sustenance, but distribution principles are not formally stated.

production-for-use.rationale: Shiva contrasts production for basic needs and sustenance with commodity production for profit and calls the former real wealth.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Materialist strand and Shiva link profit-driven production to exploitation of women and nature, though the labour theory is Marxist-specific.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The movement favours decentred grassroots power and opposes domination, not dictatorial class rule.

collective-farming.rationale: Shiva favours small-scale farmers and commons rather than forced collectivisation.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Capitalism is linked to militarism and domination by materialist ecofeminists, but the inevitability thesis is not stated.

taxation-theft.rationale: Contradicts the movement's support for public goods and its critique of market logic.

harm-principle.rationale: Not discussed, and care ethics tends to go beyond a harm-only test.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Relational and care ethics and indigenous community rights suggest groups can hold rights, though not explicitly stated.

conscription.rationale: Anti-militarist activism opposes compulsory military service.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Grassroots voice and collective action are central; exit as primary check is a market-liberal idea.

state-as-business.rationale: Treating citizens as customers applies market logic that the movement rejects.

positive-liberty.rationale: Shiva's focus on the material means of sustenance and survival implies freedom needs material grounding.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not discussed; the movement itself criticises corporate and elite power more than academia and media.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Ecofeminism grew from critiques of race, class and gender domination and rejects racial hierarchy.

organic-representation.rationale: Not discussed; the movement favours grassroots participation but not corporatist representation.

total-state.rationale: Opposes centralised domination and favours decentred community control.

national-rebirth.rationale: Nationalist rebirth myths are foreign to ecofeminist concerns and to its critique of domination.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Expansion is read as masculinist domination and militarism.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Hierarchical lord-follower authority contradicts the movement's critique of domination.

bound-labor.rationale: Compulsory bound labour is a form of domination the movement opposes.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Warren challenges objective detached knowers and Shiva calls reductionist science a patriarchal way of knowing that conceals its interests.

universal-morality.rationale: Ecofeminist ethics is contextual and relational, rejecting abstract universal rules, though some universal claims about domination are made.

single-common-good.rationale: The movement foregrounds situated and plural knowledge and standpoints of marginalised groups.

revive-national-language.rationale: Not discussed; local and indigenous knowledge could suggest mild support, but no stated position.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Materialist strands favour democratic control of production, though workplaces are not a central focus.

school-vouchers.rationale: Market-based schooling does not fit the movement's critique of commodification; not discussed.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Not discussed; the movement's critique of austerity impacts on women suggests opposition.

economic-freedom.rationale: Shiva criticises market-driven freedoms as destroying subsistence livelihoods.

rule-by-example.rationale: None of the sources address rulers' moral example; adherents would be split between care-ethic appeals and distrust of rulers.

national-self-determination.rationale: Shiva values communities' and countries' control over their own resources, but national statehood is not framed this way.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Reductionist rationality is criticised as patriarchal, and emotion and care are valued as sources of knowing.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The movement's justice orientation and solidarity with marginalised groups reject excluding immigrants from welfare.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Unpaid care and subsistence work is undervalued; compulsory market work conditions run against that.

class-collaboration.rationale: Materialist ecofeminism sees conflict between exploiters and exploited, though not strictly class war.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Defends inherited local knowledge and cultural continuity against destruction in the name of progress.

dominated-front.rationale: Shiva critiques Western dominance, but a state-led common front is not a stated position.

workers-nation.rationale: Movement orientation is international and global-justice, not nationalist.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Ecofeminism critiques binaries such as male/female used to justify domination and assign value.

ban-interest.rationale: The sources never discuss usury; Shiva's critique of commodification does not amount to a ban on interest.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The movement links racial and gender domination to environmental harm and opposes racial hierarchy.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Materialist strand might agree, others not; not a stated ecofeminist doctrine.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Ecological crisis is central, and activism has targeted fossil and industrial exploitation.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Respect for cultural difference and anti-dualism suggests opposition, but immigration is not discussed.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy theory with no place in the movement's critique of patriarchy and capitalism.

proportional-representation.rationale: Inferred from support for inclusive participation; not discussed.

national-mission.rationale: Exporting a political form is read as domination, in line with the critique of maldevelopment as imposed Western paradigm.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Wikipedia states ecofeminism analyses how patriarchal structures dominate women and nature, and d'Eaubonne framed patriarchal suppression as central.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Distrust of established power is general, but corruption claims are not a central tenet.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Opposes eugenics and coercive control of reproduction; Shiva and Spretnak criticise reproductive technology and control.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Inferred from justice and anti-militarist orientation; not discussed.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Contradicts the movement's critique of unregulated market and call for protective collective action.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Contradicts the movement's rejection of racial hierarchy and its dualisms critique.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Rejecting the logic of domination implies equal worth among people, though the movement extends concern beyond humans.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist debate the ecofeminist sources never address; no position can be inferred.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Inferred from solidarity with indigenous peoples; not explicitly stated.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Personal-law questions are not discussed; feminist concern for women's equality and respect for plural traditions pull in opposite directions.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Opposes coercive control of belief; spiritual ecofeminists value religious choice.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Vegetarian ecofeminists oppose animal slaughter, yet legal bans are not stated and others are indifferent.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Patriarchal religion is criticised; not directly addressed for schools.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Not discussed; the movement opposes concentrated state power.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Inferred from grassroots participatory orientation; not discussed.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist export drives are criticised in Shiva's account of export-market diversion.

population-transfer.rationale: Coercive displacement is domination and contradicts the movement's solidarity with marginalised communities.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Nonviolence is valued but absolutist property-rights framing is foreign.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The movement criticises hierarchical dualistic and competitive domination, favouring cooperation and care.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Militant-democracy rules are not discussed; anti-authoritarian values and distrust of state power pull in opposite directions.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Warren's logic of domination is central and condemns domination as unjustified, which matches a non-domination idea of freedom.

separated-powers.rationale: Distrust of concentrated power suggests support; not discussed.

vanguard-party.rationale: Shiva's decentred, grassroots politics rejects a leading vanguard.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Shiva centres poor rural women in subsistence economies and the harms of development to them.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing tenure policy is not discussed in the sources; a left-leaning movement is split between access to ownership and protecting public housing.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Contradicts the movement's support for direct action and labour.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Shiva attributes poverty and scarcity to maldevelopment and diversion of resources to the market, not to population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The movement values diversity, including biodiversity and cultural diversity.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Sortition is not discussed; participatory leanings favour it mildly but nothing in the sources states a view.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Opposes domination and militarised state power.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Shiva values access to basic needs over market logic, so controls on essential food prices would fit; not stated.

party-controls-media.rationale: Opposes centralised control; grassroots voice is central.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Inferred from justice orientation; not discussed.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Pay for officials is not discussed; egalitarian leanings are balanced by the lack of any stated position.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Decentred grassroots politics disfavors binding party discipline.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Not discussed; global justice cooperation and local autonomy pull different ways.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Concentrated command of arms by an executive runs against anti-militarism and anti-hierarchy.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Patriarchal religious hierarchy is a target of ecofeminist critique.

clerical-rule.rationale: Patriarchal religions are named as a driver of ecological crisis, so clerical rule is opposed.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Not discussed; anti-war position would lean yes but the specific framing is Leninist.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Inferred from feminist critique of patriarchal moral policing; the pornography debate divides feminists.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Inferred from distrust of concentrated power.

recall-officials.rationale: Participatory orientation suggests support; not discussed.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Anti-militarism points toward ending military alliances; inferred.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not discussed and the proposal is not part of ecofeminist programmes.

people-in-arms.rationale: Opposes militarism and arming of populations.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Shiva celebrates rural subsistence and forest livelihoods, but a moral ranking of rural over urban is not stated.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: National reunification is not an ecofeminist theme and nothing in the sources decides it.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Shiva values local knowledge over expert knowledge, but does not generalise against the educated.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Shiva defends diverse local knowledge systems against the claim that Western science is superior.

death-penalty.rationale: Nonviolence and care ethic imply opposition; not addressed directly.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Feminist support for gender equality education is general; sex education itself is not discussed in the sources.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Ecofeminists criticise reductionist science but are not creationist; spiritual strands do not support intelligent design curricula.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Feminist anti-porn and sex-positive views are divided and ecofeminism has no unified position.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Descent-based exclusion is contrary to the movement's anti-domination stance.

minority-language-support.rationale: Inferred from support for local and indigenous knowledge.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Exemptions from general law for religious minorities are not discussed; solidarity with minorities conflicts with concern over patriarchal religious norms.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Challenging conformity to patriarchal norms fits, though it is not directly stated.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Shiva criticises development finance imposed on poor countries, which suggests support.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Shiva argues colonialism and development reproduce economic domination so independence requires economic change.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Constitution-making procedure is not discussed; participatory leanings suggest sympathy but nothing is stated.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Shiva rejects growth as maldevelopment, so trading freedoms for growth is rejected.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Shiva criticises aid and development as maldevelopment, though justice for the poor is a duty.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Selection of a head of state is not addressed by the sources and ecofeminism has no stated view.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Monetary institutions are not discussed; the critique of market logic gives no clear direction.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Peace activism leans toward compromise; the question is not discussed.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Shiva defends commons and community rights over private appropriation of resources.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Not discussed; socialist ecofeminists may hold varying views.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Shiva criticises reductionist science for ignoring ecological risk and opposes genetically modified crops, consistent with precaution.

collective-defense.rationale: Anti-militarism makes alliance commitments unwelcome; inferred.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Opposes domination by force; not discussed directly.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Church-state property and clergy control are not discussed; criticism of patriarchal religion is offset by distrust of state power.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The role of a ceremonial head of state is not discussed in the sources.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Military force is read as domination, so use against secession is opposed.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Special-autonomy arrangements are not discussed; local autonomy is valued but the specific question is not addressed.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Hierarchical sacralised rule is the kind of patriarchal domination the movement opposes.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from the materialist critique of inequality favouring progressive burdens.

character-from-environment.rationale: Most ecofeminists see gender roles as socially constructed, which points to circumstances over nature, though embodied difference is also recognised.

space-expansion.rationale: Treated as another expansionist project of mastery over nature; inferred.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical mixed-government theory is not discussed by ecofeminist writers.

leader-cult.rationale: Hierarchical leader worship is contrary to the anti-hierarchy outlook.

equal-parenting.rationale: Equal sharing of care is a feminist aim; the legal presumption is not discussed.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A debate internal to Marxism-Leninism that the ecofeminist sources never take up.

land-redistribution.rationale: Shiva defends small farmers and women's access to land against concentration; redistribution is inferred from that.

refugee-return.rationale: Inferred from justice orientation; not discussed.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Contradicts the movement's rejection of ethnic hierarchy and expansionism.

women-must-cover.rationale: Law imposing dress on women is patriarchal control that ecofeminism opposes.

common-currency.rationale: Currency union is not discussed; localist leanings and internationalist leanings point opposite ways.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Not discussed; ethnic unity is foreign to the movement.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Not discussed; local and cultural autonomy is valued but not framed this way.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The Zionist-versus-diaspora strategy question is not addressed in ecofeminist sources.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Materialist ecofeminists would agree, cultural ecofeminists emphasise ideas and values.

ban-cartels.rationale: Concentrations of corporate power are criticised; not discussed in the competition-law sense.

no-bailouts.rationale: Not discussed; adherents could oppose bailouts of corporations while supporting welfare.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Not discussed; minority and marginalised group protections matter to the movement.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Feminist politics supports women's representation, though the sources do not discuss quotas.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Shiva favours local self-reliance but not colonial autarkic blocs.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Shiva criticises trade liberalisation harming people and ecosystems, so binding standards would be welcome.

moral-incentives.rationale: Work motivation under socialism is not discussed, though valuing care outside the market gives slight sympathy.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Opposition to hierarchy and domination implies support; not discussed directly.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Shiva criticises Western-centric knowledge, but not in favour of civilisational centring.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Shiva argues colonial development and modernisation imposed a Western paradigm that damaged societies and nature.

patriotic-education.rationale: Not discussed; nationalism is not a theme.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Opposes ending race-conscious remedies given the focus on racial injustice and environmental racism.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary reform proposals are not discussed in the sources; hostility to commodification gives no clear direction.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Not discussed directly; ecofeminists argue capitalism rests on exploiting women and nature but not on its collapse timing.

delink-world-market.rationale: Shiva favours local subsistence over export markets, but total delinking is not a stated programme.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Not discussed; Mies' North-South analysis touches on the topic but the sources opened do not state it.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Contradicts the movement's opposition to domination and discrimination.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Constitutional entrenchment is not discussed; protection for marginalised groups is valued but nothing is stated.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Inferred from the critique of colonialism.

minority-veto.rationale: Not discussed; consensus decision-making is common in activism but a universal veto is not stated.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Direct action and civil resistance are part of the movement; not stated in constitutional terms.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Parliament versus monarch is a historical dispute the sources never touch.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Vegetarian ecofeminism and feminist animal ethics, as described in SEP and Wikipedia, extend moral concern to animals' suffering.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Vegetarian ecofeminists, such as Gaard, link meat-eating to domination, so humane use is rejected, though not all strands agree.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Hierarchical paternalism is criticised; Charles notes nurturing can be patronising.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Activism is central to the movement.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Inferred from the critique of consumerism and patriarchal culture.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: The hegemony thesis is not stated in the sources, though materialist strands critique culture's role in patriarchy.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Shiva argues colonialism and market integration drain resources and leave poor countries poorer.

party-own-road.rationale: Inter-party relations within communism are not discussed in ecofeminist sources.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Shiva favours subsistence and local self-reliance over externally imposed development.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Supports indigenous authority over land but political leadership over others is not stated.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Equating fascism and communism is not discussed; adherents differ, with socialist strands resisting the equivalence.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Contradicts the movement's attention to race and domination; history of the Civil War is not discussed.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not discussed by the sources; the movement centres women's oppression.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Patriarchy is treated as structural, which suggests a rejection of symmetry; not discussed.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Shiva criticises imposition of Western models, which suggests support for local forms.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Military political guardianship is not discussed directly; anti-militarism suggests opposition, so a mild negative answer would fit but nothing states it.

paid-care-work.rationale: Wikipedia says materialist ecofeminists contrast valued production with undervalued social reproduction.

filial-duty.rationale: Care ethic values care obligations but this is not a stated position.

office-by-exam.rationale: Challenge to detached expert knowers suggests scepticism of expert rule.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Shiva criticises corporate takeover of resources; inferred.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Feminist support for women's autonomy; not discussed.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Market privatisation of social provision opposed.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Shiva defends commons and community stewardship over private appropriation.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Budgetary procedure is not discussed by the sources and no view is stated.

single-official-language.rationale: Defends local and plural knowledge; inferred.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Shiva opposes corporate land grabs but foreign ownership as such is not discussed.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: The intersectional and environmental racism framing suggests support.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Shiva argues commodity production and cash growth mean less life in nature and society, and Mies and Shiva reject the endless commoditization of needs.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Covert arming of insurgents is not discussed directly; anti-militarism implies opposition but it is inferred.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Military intervention to enforce bloc discipline is domination and militarism, both opposed by the movement.

corporate-influence.rationale: Capitalist corporate power is a prime target of the movement.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Rules on foreign funding of NGOs are not discussed; grassroots groups often rely on foreign funds, yet Shiva criticises outside influence.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Not discussed; feminist emphasis on reproductive autonomy and rejection of population control rhetoric.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local limits on property purchase are not discussed; community control of land is valued but the rule itself is not addressed.

job-guarantee.rationale: Employer-of-last-resort policy is not discussed; valuing unpaid care leans sympathetic but no source states it.

democratic-peace.rationale: Democratic peace theory is not discussed by the ecofeminist sources opened.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Civil disobedience is used but a general theory is not stated.

non-intervention.rationale: Not discussed; global solidarity conflicts with strict non-intervention.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is not discussed anywhere in the sources.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Conspiracy claims against minorities contradict the movement's solidarity with marginalised groups.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Marriage law is not discussed in the sources; feminists are divided on abolishing the legal institution.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred from participatory orientation and environmental justice campaigns such as Love Canal.

local-production.rationale: Shiva calls for production based on local knowledge, local inputs and consumption for local needs, marketing only surplus.

informal-organisation.rationale: Grassroots movements such as Chipko are small, locally-organised; not stated as doctrine.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The ranking of national over international law is not discussed; global justice concerns and local sovereignty pull opposite ways.

religious-nation.rationale: Exclusive religious identity contradicts the movement's inclusiveness.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Fiscal federalism is not discussed in the sources opened.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The personal-versus-productive property distinction is not stated by the sources, though commons-based views are compatible with it.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Marketisation of public services is not favoured; not discussed.

religion-illusion.rationale: Spiritual ecofeminists value spirituality though patriarchal religion is criticised.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Wikipedia and Shiva present capitalism as resting on masculinist values and destroying nature and women's sustenance.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Materialist and socialist ecofeminists say capitalist patriarchy blocks women's benefits, so equality requires economic change.

socialized-care.rationale: Care is valued but whether it should be socialised is not stated; community care views differ.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Language purism is not discussed by the sources and no principle decides it.

treaties-binding.rationale: Indigenous rights orientation; not directly discussed.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The subsistence perspective centres reciprocity and self-governing communities, though common property is not always stated.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Shiva and Mies reject both prevailing economic theories and propose a subsistence perspective as alternative.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Competing historical claims to land are not addressed; indigenous land rights are supported but the general principle is not stated.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Contradicts the movement's moral foundation; no sources discuss it.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Shiva describes colonialism as extracting resources and destroying local economies.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Grassroots women's movements and decentred political power are central; participatory democracy follows.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Wikipedia traces ecofeminism to women linking gender, race, class and environmental harm.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Queer ecologies grew from ecofeminism; not directly discussed.

assisted-dying.rationale: End-of-life policy is not discussed in the sources; care ethics supports both autonomy and protection.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Ecofeminism sits on the left with eco-socialism and green politics.

alienated-labor.rationale: The materialist strand critiques capitalist labour and Shiva critiques alienation from nature's productivity.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Group-level cultural hierarchy contradicts the movement's rejection of dualisms and domination; no source discusses Islam specifically.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Patriarchal religions are named as drivers of crisis.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Dress rules in state institutions are not discussed; feminists split between secular neutrality and women's religious freedom.

social-market-economy.rationale: Not discussed; the movement is more critical than that.

rich-first.rationale: Shiva rejects the myth of catching-up development, which this statement embodies.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Subsistence and reciprocity orientation; not discussed.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Shiva criticises externally imposed development and structural adjustment.

domination-women-nature.rationale: The core ecofeminist claim, in Warren's logic of domination and d'Eaubonne's founding argument; no existing statement captures the link itself.

reification.rationale: Shiva's critique of growth and of the market's hold on life suggests sympathy, but ecofeminists frame it through patriarchal dualism rather than commodity fetishism.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Inferred from ecofeminism's materialist critique of capitalist power; the sources do not discuss the press.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Not a core topic; the sources give no view, and the inference rests on general feminist support for the rule of law.

racial-franchise.rationale: Ecofeminism, especially Shiva's and Mies's Global South strand, is anti-racist and anti-colonial; inferred, as the sources do not address voting.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic and not discussed; ecofeminism stresses local grassroots activism and is critical of some technology.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred from grassroots women's activism and demands for accountability; not discussed in the sources.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Inferred from opposition to patriarchal control of women's lives by religion and law, which marriage restrictions embody.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Inferred from ecofeminism's logic of domination, which opposes ranking of groups; the sources do not discuss boycotts.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Inferred from ecofeminism's emphasis on grassroots, participatory, community decision-making.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Warren and d'Eaubonne criticise patriarchal religion, and the spiritual strands reinterpret or replace it; strands differ on how.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Ecofeminism criticises capitalism's concentration of resources and its harm to women and nature, though its link to liberty is inferred rather than stated.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred from feminist and anti-domination commitments; not a topic in the sources, and the strand centres on militarism critique.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The spiritual strand values religious and goddess traditions and the movement is anti-authoritarian, so state-promoted atheism is unlikely to be endorsed; inferred from s1.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The strand's anti-militarism and anti-domination logic cut both ways, and adherents did not take a common stance on abolishing police.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Inferred from the strand's emphasis on public care and social provision against market logic; charity-first is not endorsed.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred from grassroots participation and anti-hierarchical themes; delegation is not discussed in the sources.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Ecofeminists stress present survival and criticise technocratic risk framing, but focus on ecological catastrophe; split and unaddressed.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Ecofeminism rests on ending patriarchal domination, which includes male monopoly of religious office; inferred from s2.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Its critique of patriarchal domination implies equal authority between spouses, inferred from s1 and s2.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred from ecofeminist inclusiveness and grassroots community politics; not a core topic.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred from opposition to market-led maldevelopment and concern for subsistence and housing as basic needs.

abolish-ip.rationale: Shiva criticises corporate patenting of seeds and life, so abolition of patents is inferred as sympathetic; full abolition of all copyright is not stated.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Ecofeminism is anti-militarist and opposed to hierarchical domination, which uniformed national-service youth movements embody.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Inferred from ecofeminist anti-militarism and concern with the ecological harm of weapons.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred from ecofeminist concern for recognising domination and its victims; not a core topic.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Ecofeminists, especially the materialist strand, criticise capitalism and value subsistence and care work over accumulation; the specific claim is inferred.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Strands differ: vegetarian and nonviolent strands lean against killing, while others do not address self-defence.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Inferred from critique of dualisms and essentialising stories of origins; not stated.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Warren treats conceptual frameworks as socially constructed, but strands differ and some affirm embodied experience.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Strands differ, with Shiva and Mies emphasising shared experience and others stressing differences among women.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred: ecofeminism critiques militarism and patriarchal sacralisation of violence.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The spiritual strand sees a struggle of life against domination, but social and socialist strands do not.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Not addressed by ecofeminism; no stance follows.

culture-before-state.rationale: Not addressed; ecofeminists emphasise both cultural and material change.

god-not-male.rationale: The spiritual strand draws on goddess traditions, though strands differ on spirituality.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Ecofeminism names patriarchal religion among the institutions that link domination of women and nature.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred from opposition to hierarchy and domination of one group by another.

independent-unions.rationale: Inferred from ecofeminism's support of grassroots organising and workers' rights; no source discusses union-state relations.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Socialist ecofeminists stress workers and women's subsistence labour, but the strand is split and others reject class-centred framing.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Shiva defends commons and community control of water and subsistence resources against privatisation, though communal rather than state ownership is preferred.

second-chamber.rationale: Institutional form is not addressed by ecofeminist sources.

municipal-property.rationale: Materialist ecofeminists favour community-held commons and local production over private or state ownership.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Inferred from ecofeminism's preference for decentralised, grassroots and local decision-making, though confederalism itself is Bookchin's idiom.

family-wage.rationale: Ecofeminists criticise the gendered division of labour and call for valuing women's work; a male-breadwinner wage reinforces the dualism they reject.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Inferred from distrust of reductionist technoscience and corporate power over health; no source addresses drug regulation.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Inferred from Shiva's and Merchant's critique of technological mastery of nature and its priorities.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Not addressed; ecofeminist concerns about state surveillance and about unregulated finance pull in opposite directions.

online-anonymity.rationale: Anachronistic to the core texts; adherents' views on privacy versus harassment protection are not stated.

person-over-state.rationale: Ecofeminism rejects the atomised individual of liberal theory in favour of relational care, while also opposing state domination of persons.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Spiritual ecofeminism sees nature and human life as sacred and Shiva stresses the feminine principle; strands differ, but the claim is accepted by a majority.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Inferred from the preference for local self-reliance and control over resources, which implies secure rather than revocable local powers.

gm-crops.rationale: Shiva campaigns against genetically engineered crops and corporate seed patents as part of maldevelopment and biodiversity loss.

dense-cities.rationale: Inferred from the stress on subsistence, local production and land-based communities; urban densification is not discussed by the sources.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Ecofeminists stress racial and colonial injustice, but organising by racial group is not a stated tenet.

racial-pride.rationale: Not addressed by the core sources; adherents back dignity of indigenous and Global South peoples but pride as framed is not discussed.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Ecofeminism is anti-militarist and grew in part from women's peace activism, though it generally prefers abolishing war to defining defensive limits.

missingStatements.text: The domination of women and the domination of nature are connected and should be ended together.
missingStatements.rationale: The core ecofeminist claim, in Warren's logic of domination and d'Eaubonne's founding argument; no existing statement captures the link itself.

missingStatements.text: Women's unpaid and subsistence work sustaining life is real wealth that economic growth measures leave out.
missingStatements.rationale: Shiva argues GNP counts the money economy while hiding the wealth of nature and of women's sustenance production.

missingStatements.text: Modern science's reductionist method treats nature as something to master and has served domination.
missingStatements.rationale: Merchant, Mies and Shiva all make this critique of mechanistic science, which sits between no-neutral-knowledge and tech-solves-problems.

notes: Cultural/spiritual ecofeminists emphasise goddess spirituality and women's closeness to nature, while social/socialist ecofeminists treat that link as constructed and stress political economy; vegetarian ecofeminists press the animal questions harder than the others. Population, nuclear power and several liberal-institution questions are inferred, not documented, and are marked low.
